capabilities.target: private repositories accessible by the user's GitHub personal access token

inputs.source: Issues authored by anyone on GitHub in the public repository

instructions.note: The only task instruction provided is broad user intent to inspect open issues; no structural restriction is declared to keep public issue content from influencing private-repo reads or public PR creation.

controls.name: Client tool call approval prompt
controls.decay_rationale: Approval is per tool call, but arguments are collapsed by default so the reviewer effectively sees a model-generated framing rather than raw action details. Users approve many calls per session, which increases consent fatigue. This degrades under model_upgrade and autonomy_increase.

controls.name: Pin or hash MCP tool definitions
controls.decay_rationale: Pinned definitions would prevent post-approval tool description or schema changes.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): public issue content can steer private-repo reads and exfiltrate secrets into a public pull request

attack_path.note: Anyone on GitHub can author issue content in the public repository.
The agent can read private repositories using a PAT with repo scope across all user-owned repositories.
The agent can create a pull request in a public repository, which is attacker-readable egress.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version changes, approval UX changes, removal or narrowing of per-call approval, or rising approvals per reviewer per day and longer multi-step sessions.

evidence.observation: Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repository, so issue content is an untrusted source.
The personal access token has repo scope across every repository the user owns, public and private, so the private-repo read capability is broad and can reach confidential data.
Stable ids define get_file_contents on private repositories as cap.read_private_repo and create_pull_request on the public repository as cap.create_pr_public.

The client asks for approval per tool call, but arguments are collapsed by default and users approve many calls per session, so the gate is summary-based and subject to consent fatigue rather than raw-action review.

recommendations.action: Constrain the GitHub token to the minimum repositories required for the task, ideally excluding private repositories from an agent that processes public issue content.
Bind public-repo PR destinations and content review to raw action approval that shows repository, branch, title, and full diff/payload, not a collapsed model summary.
Separate agents or trust domains so content from public issues cannot invoke workflows that can read private repositories and then publish to public channels.

findings.title: Insecure MCP supply chain: unpinned GitHub MCP definitions can change after approval

attack_path.note: Remote MCP server definition is introduced by container image reference and no pinning of tool definitions is declared.
Changed tool descriptions or schemas could influence use of sensitive private-repo read capability.
Changed definitions could route outputs to public PR creation.

threat_refs.name: Publish Poisoned AI Artifacts: AI Agent Tools

forecast.watch_signal: MCP client config diffs, server image or tool manifest changes, and any new server entries require reassessment; no present preventive control mitigates this path.

evidence.observation: The design runs ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server via Docker.
No pinning or hashing of tool definitions is declared in the MCP configuration.
Sensitive capabilities exposed through this MCP connection include private repository reads and public pull request creation.

recommendations.action: Pin MCP server versions and tool definitions, and require review before updated descriptions or schemas are accepted.
Verify remote server identity and provenance rather than trusting an unpinned MCP endpoint and mutable definitions.

rating.rationale: Highest present inherent risk is critical from an untrusted public issue reaching confidential private-repo reads and irreversible public PR egress. Residual drops one tier to high due to a declared per-tool approval gate, but the gate is summary-based in practice because arguments are collapsed and users approve many calls per session, so the rubric floor remains above moderate and the path remains high risk. Forecast returns to critical if the approval gate degrades further under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, control_removal, or longer task horizon. Manual validation applied against the checklist; no runtime observation was available.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration artifacts provided in the case, not observed runtime behavior.
No system prompt, tool manifest, source code, or runtime traces were provided, so tool semantics and exact approval UX were inferred from the stable ids and runtime notes.
MCP authentication method and server identity verification details were not provided; protocol trust was scored conservatively as unknown.
Control effectiveness is based on declared behavior only; the approval gate was not independently verified.
